# Overview

`SpaMTP` analyses mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) and paired multi-omics data
in native Bioconductor containers. `SpaMTPdb` supplies annotation resources;
`SpaMTPData` supplies versioned experiments.

## Installation

Install a published Bioconductor version with `BiocManager::install("SpaMTP")`.
For source installation, use the companion versions required by `DESCRIPTION`.
This article uses the installed package and its bundled examples.

## Real tissue examples

This introduction follows two tissue sections from measured intensities to
spatial interpretation. Both compact datasets are bundled with SpaMTP.
The linked mouse-brain workflow adds paired RNA, regional analysis and pathways.

| Example | Measurements retained | Biological context |
|---|---|---|
| Mouse urinary bladder | 79 source-panel features at 2,210 grid locations | Ion distributions across archived tissue compartments |
| Pig fetal section | Three profile-ion windows at all 4,959 source locations | Heart-, liver- and nervous-system-associated spatial patterns |
| Mouse brain | 2,075 MSI features and 32,285 genes at all 876 archived paired locations | Striatal anatomy and intact/lesioned sides |

Small files retain tissue context: the bladder uses a regular spatial grid;
the pig example retains every source position and a prespecified ion panel.
Preparation, source checksums and selection rules are documented in
`help("vignetteData", package = "SpaMTP")`.

```{r load-package, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
```

# Mouse bladder: compartments and lipid-associated ions

## Source and spatial coverage

`bladder_demo.rds` derives from the public
[SpaMTPData bladder archive](https://zenodo.org/records/22733262).
Sampling every fourth pixel along x and y retains 2,210 of 34,840 source
locations and all 79 features in its previously selected panel. The source is
matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) imaging of a mouse
urinary-bladder section, also used in the
[Cardinal case study](https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/Cardinal3-vignettes/blob/main/Vignettes/Vignette1/case-study1-vignette.rmd).
That source workflow applies total ion current (TIC) normalization before
integrating peaks.
The archived `counts` assay contains processed panel intensities. Its original
full-spectrum totals are unavailable in this object; the separate
[raw-spectrum archive](https://zenodo.org/records/17246684) covers a subset
of the section's locations.

The stored `ssc` values are spatial shrunken-centroid classes. The
[archived SpaMTP tutorial](https://genomicsmachinelearning.github.io/SpaMTP/articles/Mouse_Urinary_Bladder.html)
interprets classes 2, 5 and 6 as adventitia, muscle and urothelium.
We retain these algorithm-derived labels as **archived compartment
interpretations**. The remaining classes stay visible.

```{r bladder-data}
bladder <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "bladder_demo.rds", package = "SpaMTP"))
stopifnot(identical(dim(bladder), c(79L, 2210L)))

compartment_names <- c(`2` = "Adventitia", `5` = "Muscle", `6` = "Urothelium")
compartment <- unname(compartment_names[as.character(bladder$ssc)])
compartment[is.na(compartment)] <- "Other SSC classes"
bladder$archived_compartment <- factor(compartment,
    levels = c(unname(compartment_names), "Other SSC classes"))
table(bladder$archived_compartment)
```

## Tissue context

`spatialCoords()` supplies original pixel coordinates. In Figure
1.\@ref(fig:bladder-compartments), colours identify the archived compartments;
the reversed y-axis follows image orientation.

```{r bladder-compartments, crop=NULL, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.8, out.width="720px", fig.cap="Mouse urinary bladder: all 2,210 retained grid locations in original pixel coordinates. Colours show the archived interpretation of SSC classes 2, 5 and 6; grey retains the other classes, including background. These algorithm-derived compartment labels summarize the archived spatial interpretation."}
bladder_xy <- as.data.frame(SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(bladder))
bladder_xy$compartment <- bladder$archived_compartment
compartment_palette <- c(Adventitia = "#3478A5", Muscle = "#D17A32",
    Urothelium = "#238774", `Other SSC classes` = "#D5DADD")
ggplot2::ggplot(bladder_xy, ggplot2::aes(x, y, colour = compartment)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.05) +
    ggplot2::coord_equal() + ggplot2::scale_y_reverse() +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = compartment_palette) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") +
    ggplot2::guides(colour = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 2,
        override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Pixel x", y = "Pixel y", colour = "Archived compartment")
```

## Preserve the source scale and select ions

Remove zero-total locations and apply the natural-log transformation
`log1p(x) = ln(1 + x)` to the archived processed intensities. This preserves the
upstream normalization for the spatial maps. The later
[panel-composition sensitivity analysis](#panel-composition-sensitivity)
checks how an additional **79-feature panel normalization** changes the
compartment comparison.

The two displayed masses were selected for their compartment-associated
patterns in the source tutorial. `which.min()` locates each nearest measured
mass. `archived_lipid_candidates` preserves the alternative candidate identities
reported in the source.

```{r bladder-normalization}
counts <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(bladder, "counts")
bladder <- bladder[, Matrix::colSums(counts) > 0]
SummarizedExperiment::assay(bladder, "logcounts") <-
    log1p(SummarizedExperiment::assay(bladder, "counts"))
mz <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(bladder)$mz
ion_rows <- vapply(c(741.53058, 798.54114),
    function(target) which.min(abs(mz - target)), integer(1))
ion_features <- rownames(bladder)[ion_rows]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
    measured_mz = round(mz[ion_rows], 5),
    archived_candidates = SummarizedExperiment::rowData(bladder)$
        archived_lipid_candidates[ion_rows]), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Spatial distributions and regional summaries

`plotSpatialFeature()` reads the selected features from `logcounts`.
`pointSize` controls marker size; `combine = FALSE` returns separate plots
for adding axes and compact horizontal colour bars. Each ion in Figure
1.\@ref(fig:bladder-spatial) has its own scale.

```{r bladder-spatial, crop=NULL, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.7, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Two measured bladder ions across the retained nonzero grid locations. Colour shows log1p of the archived processed intensity; each panel has an independent colour scale. The source workflow applied TIC normalization before peak integration. Positions and orientation match the compartment map."}
bladder_plots <- plotSpatialFeature(bladder, features = ion_features,
    assayName = "logcounts", labels = sprintf("m/z %.5f", mz[ion_rows]),
    pointSize = 1.1, combine = FALSE)
bladder_plots <- lapply(bladder_plots, function(p) p +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") +
    ggplot2::guides(colour = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(
        title.position = "top", barwidth = grid::unit(3.6, "cm"))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Pixel x", y = "Pixel y", colour = "Archived intensity (log1p)"))
cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = bladder_plots, ncol = 2)
```

SM, PA, PC and PE denote sphingomyelin, phosphatidic acid, phosphatidylcholine
and phosphatidylethanolamine.

The table uses every retained nonzero location in each named compartment.
`detected_percent` is the percentage with archived intensity above zero;
`median_log1p` summarizes the displayed signal.

```{r bladder-regional-summary}
input <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(bladder, "counts")
normalized <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(bladder, "logcounts")
regional_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unname(compartment_names), function(group) {
    pixels <- which(bladder$archived_compartment == group)
    data.frame(compartment = group, pixels = length(pixels),
        mz = round(mz[ion_rows], 5),
        median_log1p = apply(normalized[ion_rows, pixels, drop = FALSE], 1, median),
        detected_percent = 100 * Matrix::rowMeans(input[ion_rows, pixels, drop = FALSE] > 0))
}))
knitr::kable(regional_summary, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Panel-composition sensitivity {#panel-composition-sensitivity}

An abundant ion contributes to the denominator of panel normalization.
Here, the two additional scales divide each intensity by either the complete
panel total or the total after excluding m/z 741.53058, then multiply by 10,000
and apply `log1p`. The table compares compartment medians for m/z 798.54114.

```{r bladder-normalization-sensitivity}
panel <- normalizeSMData(bladder, "LogNormalize", verbose = FALSE)
reduced_total <- Matrix::colSums(input[-ion_rows[1], , drop = FALSE])
stopifnot(all(reduced_total > 0))
scales <- list(
    `Archived input` = as.numeric(normalized[ion_rows[2], ]),
    `79-feature panel` = as.numeric(
        SummarizedExperiment::assay(panel, "logcounts")[ion_rows[2], ]),
    `Panel excluding m/z 741.53058` = log1p(
        as.numeric(input[ion_rows[2], ]) / reduced_total * 1e4))
normalization_sensitivity <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(scales), function(scale) {
    values <- scales[[scale]]
    urothelium <- median(values[bladder$archived_compartment == "Urothelium"])
    muscle <- median(values[bladder$archived_compartment == "Muscle"])
    data.frame(scale = scale, urothelium = urothelium, muscle = muscle,
        median_difference = urothelium - muscle)
}))
stopifnot(all(normalization_sensitivity$median_difference > 0))
knitr::kable(normalization_sensitivity, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

The urothelium-minus-muscle difference is
`r round(normalization_sensitivity$median_difference[1], 3)` on the archived
log1p scale, `r round(normalization_sensitivity$median_difference[2], 3)` after
panel normalization and
`r round(normalization_sensitivity$median_difference[3], 3)` after excluding
m/z 741.53058 from the panel total. The direction persists across these scales;
the magnitude depends on the denominator. Compartment differences therefore
support a spatial distribution hypothesis within this section.

The archive lists
SM/PA alternatives for m/z 741.53058 and PC/PE alternatives for m/z 798.54114.
These patterns motivate lipid-localization hypotheses; exact lipid species
require additional chemical evidence. The comparison describes one bladder section.

The [companion workflow](SpaMTP_Companion_Workflow.html) queries these same
ions against a versioned RaMP database and retains candidate ambiguity.

# Pig fetal section: organ-associated ion patterns

## Prespecified windows across the complete source section

`pig_demo.rds` derives from the public
[pig fetal dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/17246555), acquired by
desorption electrospray ionization (DESI) on a Thermo LTQ instrument.
It retains all 4,959 source tissue locations.
The [Cardinal segmentation tutorial](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/data/experiment/vignettes/CardinalWorkflows/inst/doc/MSI-segmentation.html)
associates m/z 187.36 with heart, 537.08 with liver, and 840.43 with brain and
spinal cord. These associations describe source-reported ion-localization
patterns; organ labels and chemical identities require independent validation.

Each row sums original profile bins within **±0.5 m/z** of one target.
`total_ion_current` was calculated from all 10,200 original mass bins before
subsetting. Use that stored total when normalizing; dividing by the three
selected windows would change the biological comparison. `source_bins` reports
how many original profile bins contribute to each window.

```{r pig-data}
pig <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "pig_demo.rds", package = "SpaMTP"))
stopifnot(identical(dim(pig), c(3L, 4959L)))
window_intensity <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(pig, "counts")
SummarizedExperiment::assay(pig, "logcounts") <- log1p(
    sweep(window_intensity, 2, pig$total_ion_current, "/") * 1e4)
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(pig))[
    , c("target_mz", "window_lower", "window_upper", "source_bins")],
    row.names = FALSE)
```

## Spatial interpretation

All three panels in Figure 1.\@ref(fig:pig-spatial) use the same 4,959 source
tissue coordinates. The source-selected
signals occupy different anatomical areas across the complete section.

```{r pig-spatial, fig.width=10, fig.height=5, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Pig fetal DESI section: three prespecified profile-ion windows at all 4,959 source tissue positions. Each window sums bins within ±0.5 m/z of the title mass. Colour shows log1p(window intensity / full-spectrum TIC × 10,000), with an independent scale per panel. Heart, liver and brain/spinal-cord associations are source interpretations from the Cardinal tutorial."}
pig_plots <- plotSpatialFeature(pig, features = rownames(pig),
    assayName = "logcounts", pointSize = 0.6, combine = FALSE,
    labels = c("m/z 187.36", "m/z 537.08", "m/z 840.43"))
contexts <- c("Heart-associated", "Liver-associated", "Brain / spinal cord")
pig_plots <- lapply(seq_along(pig_plots), function(i) pig_plots[[i]] +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(25, 50, 75, 100)) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(6, 10, 6, 6)) +
    ggplot2::guides(colour = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(
        title.position = "top", barwidth = grid::unit(3.2, "cm"))) +
    ggplot2::labs(subtitle = contexts[i], x = "Pixel x", y = "Pixel y",
        colour = "TIC-normalized log1p"))
cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = pig_plots, ncol = 3)
```

This three-window panel demonstrates spatial interpretation. Peak discovery,
clustering and enrichment require the broader source spectra and appropriate
feature coverage, available as `SpaMTPData::spaMTPData("pig_fetus_cardinal",
version = "1.1.0")`.

# Mouse brain: paired MSI and RNA

The [end-to-end workflow](End_to_End_Workflow.html) uses all 876 locations in
the archived striatal selection from a mouse specimen in a
6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) lesion model
([GSM7392311](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM7392311)).
It relates measured m/z 400.14659 and the genes `Penk` and `Tac1` to anatomy
and the recorded intact/lesioned sides, then demonstrates regional summaries
and pathway analysis. The archived striatal selection follows the MSI clusters
used in the original analysis.

The [data-access guide](Modern_Data_Access.html) introduces public accessors
using this same real paired experiment. The first load retrieves its pinned
SpaMTPData resource unless a verified local or cached copy is available.

# Native containers and raw data

## Data locations

| Data | Container or accessor |
|---|---|
| Raw, unequal-axis or file-backed spectra | Cardinal `MSImagingArrays` / `MSImagingExperiment` |
| Aligned MSI intensities | `assay(spe, "counts")` |
| Masses and annotation candidates | `rowData(spe)` |
| Tissue labels and sample metadata | `colData(spe)` |
| Pixel coordinates and optical images | `spatialCoords(spe)` and `imgData(spe)` |
| Paired transcriptome | `altExp(spe, "SPT")` |

For custom binned data, assay rows represent measured mass features and columns
represent locations. Store numeric masses in `rowData(spe)$mz` and keep coordinate
rows in the same order as assay columns. Retain tissue-section identifiers in
`sample_id` and animal or donor identifiers in `colData()` for analyses across
biological samples.

## Raw imzML processing

For your own files, keep the `.ibd` companion available while file-backed
processing runs. `memory = FALSE` leaves spectra on disk; `normalizeSMData()`
queues Cardinal TIC normalization. `binSpaMTP()` executes processing and creates
a common mass axis at the requested resolution. Set resolution to suit the
instrument and analytical goal. The small simulation below uses 16 pixels and
0.1 m/z bins to demonstrate file creation, deferred processing and conversion.
The [Cardinal guide](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/Cardinal/inst/doc/Cardinal3-guide.html)
describes acquisition-specific preprocessing.

```{r raw-imzml, message=FALSE}
set.seed(1, kind = "L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
simulated <- Cardinal::simulateImage(preset = 1, npeaks = 4,
    dim = c(4, 4), centroided = TRUE, continuous = FALSE,
    SAR = FALSE, verbose = FALSE, BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam())
imzml <- tempfile(fileext = ".imzML")
Cardinal::writeImzML(simulated, imzml, bundle = FALSE, verbose = FALSE,
    BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam())
raw <- Cardinal::readImzML(imzml, memory = FALSE,
    as = "MSImagingArrays", verbose = FALSE)
raw <- normalizeSMData(raw, verbose = FALSE)
spe <- binSpaMTP(raw, resolution = 0.1, units = "mz")
stopifnot(methods::is(spe, "SpatialExperiment"), ncol(spe) == 16L,
    all(is.finite(SummarizedExperiment::assay(spe, "counts"))))
dim(spe)
```

For binned data, `asCardinal()` and standard S4 coercion preserve the intensity
matrix and coordinates. This evaluated example uses the real bladder object.

```{r cardinal-coercion}
cardinal <- asCardinal(bladder)
stopifnot(methods::is(cardinal, "MSImagingExperiment"),
    identical(dim(cardinal), dim(bladder)))
```
